category_title: Successful readers who focus on text and meaning-making
minimal_context: The student is participating in a whole-class explicit phonics lesson on decoding rules and digraphs.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's look at the board and practice our phonics rules for digraphs.

STUDENT: I’m not too big on reading, but I love books.

TUTOR: We need to practice breaking these words apart first.

STUDENT: Phonics is really boring, but it helps you to read.

TUTOR: Please pay attention to me while I explain how to code these words.

STUDENT: (Turns away from the teacher and focuses on reading the posters and charts on the wall instead of attending to the instruction.)

options.A: Withhold attention when the student engages in the off-task behavior of reading the classroom posters.
options.B: Allow the student to work at her own pace on the phonics task and take breaks.
options.C: Use a question-answer format to identify sounds, count sounds, define digraphs, and apply coding marks.
options.D: Provide a gentle touch on the student's shoulder to redirect her attention to the phonics instruction.
